props.doc:
Run one report and return rows plus the metadata an export needs.

Each report checks its own declared permission before it runs, so adding one
to the catalogue cannot accidentally widen who can read the data underneath.
Every query is parameterised and org-scoped like any other.
props.name: build_report

props.code:
from soar.identity.rbac import require_permission
from soar.incidents.timeline import read as timeline_read
from soar.intel.mitre import coverage
from soar.platform.ids import now_iso

catalogue = report_catalogue()
spec = catalogue.get(kind)
if spec is None:
    raise KeyError("no report named %r" % kind)
require_permission(principal, spec["permission"])

org_id = principal["org_id"]
try:
    days = max(1, min(int(filters.get("days", 30)), 400))
except (TypeError, ValueError):
    days = 30
window = str(days)

if kind == "incident":
    incident_id = filters.get("incident_id")
    if not incident_id:
        raise ValueError("the incident report needs an incident_id")
    rows = db.query("SELECT * FROM incident WHERE id = %s AND org_id = %s",
                    [incident_id, org_id], org_id)
    if not rows:
        raise KeyError("no such incident")
    data = {
        "summary": rows[0],
        "timeline": timeline_read(db, org_id, incident_id),
        "entities": db.query(
            "SELECT entity_kind, entity_id, role FROM incident_entity "
            "WHERE incident_id = %s", [incident_id], org_id),
        "indicators": db.query(
            "SELECT i.type, i.value, i.verdict, i.score FROM incident_indicator ii "
            "JOIN indicator i ON i.id = ii.indicator_id WHERE ii.incident_id = %s",
            [incident_id], org_id),
        "executions": db.query(
            "SELECT label, status, started_at, duration_ms FROM execution "
            "WHERE incident_id = %s", [incident_id], org_id),
        "approvals": db.query(
            "SELECT a.action_key, a.risk_level, a.status, a.decided_at, "
            "string_agg(d.decider_id, ', ') AS deciders FROM approval a "
            "LEFT JOIN approval_decision d ON d.approval_id = a.id "
            "WHERE a.incident_id = %s GROUP BY a.id", [incident_id], org_id),
        "ai": db.query(
            "SELECT kind, structured, confidence, accepted_by, created_at "
            "FROM ai_analysis WHERE incident_id = %s", [incident_id], org_id),
    }
    return {"kind": kind, "title": spec["title"], "sections": data,
            "generated_at": now_iso()}

QUERIES = {
    "response_actions": (
        "SELECT at, action, coalesce(target_label, target_id) AS target, "
        "coalesce(actor_label, actor_id) AS actor, on_behalf_of_id AS approver, "
        "result FROM audit_event WHERE org_id = %s "
        "AND action LIKE 'response.%%' "
        "AND at > now() - (%s || ' days')::interval ORDER BY at DESC"),
    "automation_metrics": (
        "SELECT p.name AS playbook, count(*) AS runs, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.status = 'succeeded') AS succeeded, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.status = 'failed') AS failed, "
        "percentile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY e.duration_ms) AS median_ms "
        "FROM execution e JOIN playbook p ON p.id = e.playbook_id "
        "WHERE e.org_id = %s AND e.started_at > now() - (%s || ' days')::interval "
        "GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY runs DESC"),
    "analyst_activity": (
        "SELECT coalesce(actor_label, actor_id) AS analyst, "
        "count(DISTINCT target_id) FILTER (WHERE target_kind = 'incident') "
        "  AS incidents_touched, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'approval.decided') AS approvals, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'incident.note') AS notes "
        "FROM audit_event WHERE org_id = %s AND actor_kind = 'user' "
        "AND at > now() - (%s || ' days')::interval "
        "GROUP BY analyst ORDER BY incidents_touched DESC"),
    "detection_metrics": (
        "SELECT a.source, count(*) AS alerts, "
        "count(DISTINCT a.incident_id) AS incidents, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE i.resolution = 'true_positive') AS true_positive, "
        "count(*) FILTER (WHERE i.resolution = 'false_positive') AS false_positive "
        "FROM alert a LEFT JOIN incident i ON i.id = a.incident_id "
        "WHERE a.org_id = %s AND a.observed_at > now() - (%s || ' days')::interval "
        "GROUP BY a.source ORDER BY alerts DESC"),
}

if kind == "integration_health":
    rows = db.query(
        "SELECT name, connector_id AS connector, health, last_check_at, last_error "
        "FROM integration WHERE org_id = %s ORDER BY health, name", [org_id], org_id)
elif kind == "mitre_coverage":
    rows = coverage(db, org_id, days)
else:
    rows = db.query(QUERIES[kind], [org_id, window], org_id)

return {"kind": kind, "title": spec["title"],
        "columns": spec.get("columns", []), "rows": rows,
        "window_days": days, "generated_at": now_iso(),
        "generated_for": principal.get("id")}

props.doc:
Render a report and store it in the object store, returning its key.

The bytes go to the object store rather than down the response, so a large
export cannot be a memory spike on the API node and the artefact is the same
one an auditor can fetch later by key. The export is audited: who exported
what, when.

JSON and CSV are implemented. PDF is deliberately a print-ready HTML document
rather than a bundled renderer - a headless browser is a second attack surface
and a large dependency, and the SOCs that need signed PDFs generally have a
document service already.
props.name: export_report

props.code:
from soar.audit.log import record as audit_record
from soar.identity.rbac import require_permission
from soar.platform.runtime import services
from soar.storage.objects import object_key

import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json

require_permission(principal, "reports.export")
report = build_report(db, principal, kind, filters)
org_id = principal["org_id"]

if format == "json":
    body = json.dumps(report, indent=2, default=str)
    content_type = "application/json"
elif format == "csv":
    rows = report.get("rows") or []
    columns = report.get("columns") or (list(rows[0].keys()) if rows else [])
    buffer = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.DictWriter(buffer, fieldnames=columns, extrasaction="ignore")
    writer.writeheader()
    for row in rows:
        writer.writerow({c: row.get(c) for c in columns})
    body = buffer.getvalue()
    content_type = "text/csv"
elif format in ("pdf", "html"):
    body = report_html(report)
    content_type = "text/html"
else:
    raise ValueError("unsupported export format %r" % format)

payload = body.encode("utf-8")
digest = hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
key = object_key(org_id, "report", digest)
services()["objects"].put(key, body)

audit_record(db, {
    "org_id": org_id, "actor_kind": principal.get("kind", "user"),
    "actor_id": principal.get("id"), "action": "report.export",
    "target_kind": "report", "target_id": kind,
    "after": {"format": format, "sha256": digest, "bytes": len(payload)},
    "result": "success",
})

return {"object_key": key, "sha256": digest, "bytes": len(payload),
        "content_type": content_type,
        "note": ("print this page to PDF; the platform does not bundle a "
                 "renderer") if format == "pdf" else None}

Every value is HTML-escaped on the way in. A report is the one artefact that
leaves the platform and gets opened somewhere else, so incident content - which
is attacker-influenceable - must not be able to carry markup into it.
